title: Mammals produce cyclo-octasulfur to suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the study's only public deposit, PRIDE (PRoteomics IDEntifications database) PXD080540, and listed all 7 files (765 MB total: one 637 MB Agilent .d raw archive, a 121 MB peak list, and small result tables). Downloaded and opened both small CSVs: results.csv has 4,566 rows of unnamed mass-spectrometry features (m/z, retention time, peak height, area) from a single run named 3T3-L1_LD.d, with the protein-name columns empty; results-coverage.csv has exactly 4 rows (mouse eNOS, perilipin, SQR, caveolin-1) with a 'Confirmation Status' and '% coverage'. Also confirmed the Science article page returns HTTP 403, and that Europe PMC has no full text, no supplement and no text-mined accessions for this PMID (42784683).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the actual biology — millimolar S8 (cyclo-octasulfur, an eight-membered sulfur ring) in mitochondrial membranes and lipid droplets, S8 levels in human breast tumour versus normal tissue, exhaled-breath measurements, Raman microscopy images, 4-HNE lipid-peroxidation readouts, and the mouse osteoarthritis injection experiment — comes only from the abstract and press coverage. None of those measurements are in any public file I could reach.

a1_downloadable.note: The one deposited dataset (PRIDE PXD080540) downloads freely, but it covers a single side experiment. The paper's actual measurements live in Science supplementary tables behind a paywall (article page returns HTTP 403; no PubMed Central copy, no Zenodo/Dryad/Metabolomics Workbench record found).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no label column anywhere. results.csv is a list of unidentified mass-spectrometry peaks; the only outcome-like column is 'Confirmation Status' in a 4-row file. Any prediction target (S8 concentration, ferroptosis sensitivity, tumour versus normal) would have to be built from scratch from figures we cannot access.

a3_inputs_present.note: No model inputs are present: no sequences, no SMILES, no expression matrix, no spectra in a usable labelled form. The 4,566 feature rows carry m/z and retention time only, with the sequence-name field blank for nearly all rows.

a4_units_stated.note: Units in the deposited CSV are conventional and clear (m/z for mass, minutes for retention time, counts for height/area, % for sequence coverage) — checked in the file headers.

a5_enough_rows.note: The experimental unit here is a sample, and there is exactly one sample (one LC-Q-TOF run of lipid droplets from 3T3-L1 mouse adipocytes), with 4 labelled target-protein rows. Far below the ~400-row minimum even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.5 MB of result tables; 765 MB if you also took the raw run
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem. The small tables opened instantly; the 637 MB Agilent raw archive is raw mass spectrometry, which project rules say not to download anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to contradict: the deposit's header says '4566 found' and the file contains 4,566 feature rows plus 4 header lines, which is internally consistent. The paper's own counts could not be checked without the paywalled text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable, which is itself the failure. The 'Confirmation Status' values come from Agilent MassHunter BioConfirm software matching peaks to four chosen sequences, so the only outcome-like column in the public data is software output on a target list, not an independent measurement of anything we would want to predict.

existing_models.name: DeepFerr (deep-learning predictor of ferroptosis state from the expression of 11 ferroptosis regulator genes), plus many 'ferroptosis-related gene signature' prognostic models
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved — I only saw search-result summaries, not the papers, so I record no numbers and no split.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle a lipid-droplet proteome list could be joined to UniProt or the LD (lipid droplet) proteome literature on gene symbol, but the deposited file has no protein identifications to join on.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the public file contains unidentified peaks from one sample, so there is nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: The deposit itself is effectively a positive control for the authors' own claim (perilipin, a lipid-droplet coat protein, confirmed at 83% coverage), but it is a one-sample confirmation, not a dataset a model could be controlled on.
controls.negative_control: None available — no replicates, no conditions, no shufflable labels.
controls.external_validation: None — no second dataset from this study and no public resource measuring S8 in cells or tissues.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: the only public data is a single mass-spectrometry run with no labels, so any model would be fitting four software-derived confirmation calls.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use cell and tissue molecular profiles to predict how much elemental sulfur (S8) a cell stores and how resistant it is to lipid-damage cell death.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need paired profiles (gene or protein expression, lipid content) and measured S8 per cell line or tissue sample. Verified number of such paired examples in public data: zero; the single deposit has one sample.
plain_idea.predict: S8 concentration (millimolar) or ferroptosis sensitivity, where the truth would come from the authors' mass spectrometry using a polyaromatic capsule that traps S8, or from Raman microscopy — neither of which is deposited anywhere public.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If S8 really gates ferroptosis, redox and cancer-metabolism labs would want to know which cells are S8-rich before testing ferroptosis-inducing drugs; but nothing in the released data lets anyone build that.

more_or_better_data.why: Our usable public data is one mass-spectrometry run of 4,566 unidentified peaks; existing ferroptosis gene-signature models were trained on hundreds to thousands of tumour transcriptomes from TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) and similar cohorts.

confidence_score.why: A single run with no replicates gives no way to estimate measurement noise, so per-prediction confidence cannot be calibrated.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant here — the existing ferroptosis models address a different task (prognosis from expression), and we have no data on this paper's task to compete with them on.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on the first condition: there is no baseline to run and no feature/label table to extend, because the paper's measurements were never deposited.

ml_idea: The appealing idea was to predict cellular S8 content or ferroptosis resistance from molecular profiles, using this paper as the label source. It is not buildable: the only public artefact is PRIDE PXD080540, a one-sample lipid-droplet proteomics run whose purpose was to show that endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) sits on lipid droplets. The paper's quantitative S8 data, Raman spectra and animal results are paywalled supplementary figures.

effort.compute_note: Measured directly: the two result CSVs total 0.44 MB and opened in under a second with Python's csv module. No modelling workload exists to estimate.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the samples in the only public deposit. One run, 4 labelled target rows — that kills it in five minutes, and it did.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A on A1, A2, A3, A5 and A8, all verified in the files rather than inferred from the paper. The study deposited exactly one dataset (PRIDE PXD080540), a single LC-Q-TOF run of lipid droplets from mouse 3T3-L1 adipocytes: 4,566 rows of unidentified mass-spectrometry peaks and a 4-row table confirming four target proteins. Every quantity the paper is actually about — millimolar S8 in mitochondria and lipid droplets, tumour versus normal breast tissue, exhaled breath, the osteoarthritis model — sits in Science supplementary material that is paywalled (HTTP 403) with no PubMed Central copy and no Zenodo, Dryad or Metabolomics Workbench record. This is a beautiful piece of chemistry with no public data to model; if the supplementary tables ever become open, the S8-versus-tissue measurements would be worth a second look, but the sample counts implied by the press coverage (a handful of tissues and patients) would almost certainly still fail A5.
